title: Operational safety net design walkthrough and team pulse
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
A working walkthrough of the operational safety-net concept for model-serving SLOs. This doc is intentionally lightweight: mix of design notes, simulation plans, and a team pulse checklist so on-call and product owners can quickly align. Not a final playbook yet — meant for cross-functional review and experiments.

High-level problem we solve:
- When capacity/latency degrades or models regress, customers must still get useful responses without violating critical SLAs.
- We need predictable fallback behaviors, transparent billing/telemetry, and an easy way to test them in staging.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Clear safety-net flow for 3 degradation classes (latency spike, token-error spike, model-quality regression).
- Automated routing fallback from primary model -> lighter/quantized variant -> cached response -> canned message.
- SLO definitions per class + observable alerts that are actionable.
- Simulation harness that can reproduce 95th/99th percentile latency scenarios and the fallback transitions.

Stakeholders and roles (working list):
- Owner: Samira Ghosh (eng-sre)
- Runtime: Miguel Alvarez (serving-runtime) - implement routing hooks
- Product: Priya Patel (product-hosted-api) - define customer-facing degradations
- Observability: Leah Wong (observability) - metrics/alerting contract
- Solutions/CS: Tom Becker - customer impact scenarios + docs

Design sketch (quick):
1) Detection layer: anomaly detector on P95 latency, token error rate, and semantic-quality regressions (uses eval set callbacks).
2) Decision policy: priority list + cooldown + circuit-breaker window. Example: if P95 latency > 1200ms for 2m -> open latency circuit for that model pool.
3) Fallback ladder: route -> quantized-variant (same family, smaller tokens) -> shorter-max-tokens variant -> cached prefix lookup -> canned low-quality-safe response.
4) Billing/telemetry: tag routed requests with "fallback_reason" and expose per-customer fallback-rates in console.

SLO drafts (for discussion):
- Availability SLO: 99.9% successful responses (success = model returned structured output w/o internal errors)
- Latency SLO: P95 < 450ms for user-facing small requests; P99 < 1200ms (applies per route/model pair)
- Quality guardrail: % of responses failing eval-run checks < 0.5% over a 1h window
Notes: these are intentionally conservative and need product signoff.

Simulation plan (short):
- Synthetic traffic harness runs 30m load with realistic token distributions (chat vs completion).
- Inject slow kernel on a subset of GPUs to simulate degraded capacity.
- Inject model regression by swapping model weights in staging to a degraded checkpoint and measure fallback ladder.
- Measure time-to-fallback, percent of traffic affected, and billing delta.
- Runbook test: perform tabletop where SRE triggers simulated degradation and product ops coordinates customer-facing comms.

Telemetry & alerts (must-haves):
- Per-model P50/P95/P99 latency, per-route error-rate, fallback-rate by reason, fallback-ladder-step counts.
- Alert: latency P95 > threshold for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> page on-call.
- Alert: fallback_rate_by_customer > 1% for 10m -> SE + CS notify.

Runbook excerpt (quick checklist for on-call):
- Step 0: Identify whether the signal is latency, errors, or quality. Check dashboard filter by model and region.
- Step 1: If latency -> confirm autoscaler activity and queue length; if autoscaler healthy and latency remains, flip routing to secondary pool (manual toggle) and monitor fallback metrics.
- Step 2: If errors -> check model logs for OOMs or token errors; if transient, increase retries and monitor; if persistent, route to quantized variant.
- Step 3: If quality -> run eval set, open incident if regression confirmed, rollback to prior pinned version and notify product.
- Post-incident: add synthetic test to nightly safety-net harness.

Team pulse & quick asks (notes to self):
- This needs a 60-minute sync with runtime+observability+product to agree on detection thresholds. -> ACTION: schedule with Miguel/Leah/Priya.
- Need sample customer scenarios from CS (Tom) to validate canned responses UX.
- Decide billing exposure: should we show fallback as a separate line-item or fold into normal usage? (Ops finance input needed).
- Priority list for staging tests: latency-circuit -> quantized-variant -> caching behavior -> canned-message UX.

Open questions / risks (brainstorm):
- Risk: too aggressive fallbacks can degrade quality silently and erode trust. How do we surface this to customers?
- Risk: caching prefixes may leak PII if not scrubbed; need privacy audit for cached content.
- Which customers get automatic fallbacks vs. opt-in? (enterprise vs. free tier?)
- How to test semantic-quality fallback automatically without human review? (Need eval thresholds and synthetic prompts).

Quick timeline (30/60/90):
- 30d: align on SLO drafts, detection thresholds; land minimal fallback ladder in staging (quantized variant route).
- 60d: build synthetic traffic harness for two canonical routes; run 3 end-to-end experiments and refine alerts.
- 90d: integrate fallback telemetry into Console dashboards; draft customer comms for opt-in and enable enterprise controls.

Backlog / TODOs (short):
- [ ] Schedule threshold sync (owner: Samira)
- [ ] Create staging test plan and infra ticket (REL-120) (owner: Miguel)
- [ ] Privacy review for caching (owner: Leah)
- [ ] UX copy for canned degraded responses (owner: Tom)
- [ ] Add synthetic prompt set for quality checks (owner: Priya)

References & quick links:
- Confluence: operational-safety-net design (linked_artifacts above)
- Jira tickets: SRE-342 (fallback policy prototype), REL-120 (staging harness)
- Code PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2123 (routing hooks prototype)

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Could we expose an "observability-only" mode where customers see predicted fallbacks before they happen? That might reduce churn.
- Consider a monthly "fallback transparency" report for enterprise customers to explain billing and quality impact.

If you read this and want to edit: add your quick experiment ideas under "Simulation plan" and flag any thresholds you think are optimistic. This doc will become the central scratchpad for the first 90d experiment cycle.
